newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC/China Light link would make sense - analysts.
newsitem.headline: CITIC/China Light link would make sense - analysts.

text.p: A link between CITIC Pacific Ltd and China Light and Power Co Ltd would fall right in line with CITIC's diversification strategy while giving China Light a partner in China, analysts said on Tuesday.
Trading in the shares of both companies was suspended on Tuesday, prompting rumours that CITIC may buy a stake in China Light, brokers said.
"It is in line with CITIC's strategy," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment. "Both of them have infrastructure projects in China."
Kelvin Tang, analyst at ImPac Asset Management, said CITIC Pacific had been caught up in the aviation industry over the last year but had not expanded its infrastructure business.

Meanwhile, other red chip companies had been talking about asset injections. "If you look at CITIC Pacific's business nature, it is time for the company to diversify its business into other areas," said Tang.
"It is the biggest red chip in Hong Kong and with such a strong connection in China, it would be a good move for the company to acquire a very strong background in infrastructure."
Tony Yung, research manager at Tai Fook Securities, said the deal would benefit both parties.
"CITIC can make use of China Light's power projects expertise for its infrastructural projects, and CITIC can in return help China Light to secure more projects," Yung said.
Tang at ImPac said infrastructure did not account for a substantial part of CITIC's earnings and a China Light stake would provide it with a way of strengthening its recurrent earnings base.
"I think it is a very long term strategic move for the company (CITIC) to try to expand itself in the infrastructure business," Tang said.

"Infrastructure currently does not account for a substantial earnings stream for the company but if it acquires China Light it has the potential to expand its infrastructure business in China and expand its earnings power," said Tang.
Meanwhile, China Light could use CITIC to expand in China, another analyst said.

"We have held the view that it makes a lot of sense for China Light and Power to find a Chinese partner like CITIC Pacific because the company is well capitalised but is very slow in terms of expanding into China," he said.
He said China Light's slow progress in China indicated that the company was having problems with its mainland plans.

"This company has difficulties in achieving growth and going forward. The business in the territory will remain quite slow so they really need to expand into countries like China to expand growth," the analyst said.
Analysts said a stake sale could take different forms, such as an issue of new shares, share swap or acquisition from another China Light shareholder.
China Light was owned 14.45 percent by Hesko Ltd, 10.01 percent by Mikado Investment Ltd, and 8.63 percent by R.J. McAulay as of April 1996.
Shares in China Light rose HK$0.60 to HK$33.70 on Monday and CITIC Pacific added HK$1.10 to HK$39.50.
Both companies declined to comment on the trading suspensions but said there would be announcements later.
